claims: Roughly three dozen countries, primarily in the Americas, grant unconditional birthright citizenship (jus soli) to nearly everyone born on their soil.
The U.S. grants unconditional birthright citizenship (jus soli) to nearly everyone born on its soil.
Canada grants unconditional birthright citizenship (jus soli) to nearly everyone born on its soil.
Mexico grants unconditional birthright citizenship (jus soli) to nearly everyone born on its soil.
Argentina grants unconditional birthright citizenship (jus soli) to nearly everyone born on its soil.
Brazil grants unconditional birthright citizenship (jus soli) to nearly everyone born on its soil.
Unconditional birthright citizenship (jus soli) is rare in Europe and Asia.
Citizenship in Europe and Asia is usually based on parentage (jus sanguinis).
